content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.67 to +1.00) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.33 or 0.00) — model ignores downside risk.
- Lagging forecasts often overreact to recent highs — model delays mean reversion, leading to overcorrection later.
- When sentiment is mixed (e.g., 0.33/0.67 alternations), model tends to smooth too much, missing short-term volatility.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) and underestimates late (last 5–7 days) — adjust for asymmetric bias.
- If sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.67), model should reduce forecast slope to avoid “over-optimism”.
- If sentiment shows strong downward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive -0.33), model should increase downward bias, not just reduce peak.
